subject.implementation: Scripts-first driver (replaces OpenClaw-mediated agent retired in WP09)
subject.invocation: /usr/bin/python3 /home/claude/kg-automation/scripts/doc_audit/run.py (systemd user unit felix-doc-auditor.service triggered by .timer OnCalendar=hourly)

measurements.description: Tick exits cleanly with no signals to process (queue blocked on pending decisions, no new audits, no drift events past cursor).
Tick processed an audit and produced one or more docs-debt issues without applying a code edit.
Tick processed an audit that produced a Tier-A auto-commit (typically a frontmatter last_validated bump) plus follow-up actions.

comparison_with_pre_rework.weighting_basis: Pre-rework observed mix was 28 empty / 4 debt_only / 2 tier_a_apply (mix-biased empty due to blocked queue). For NFR-001 acceptance, hold per-outcome reductions as the primary comparator; weighted average is supplementary.

methodology.summary: The scripts-first driver writes a per-tick `last-tick.json` artifact (overwritten each tick) plus a deterministic SUMMARY stdout line captured by systemd journal. Token counts live under `judgment.input_tokens`, `judgment.cache_hit_input_tokens`, and `judgment.output_tokens` (see contracts/tick-signal.contract.md). The post-rework measurement either (a) walks an archive of `last-tick.json` snapshots (operator must collect — `last-tick.json` is current-state-only, so the collection happens by snapshotting after each natural tick), or (b) parses SUMMARY lines from the journal via `journalctl --user -u felix-doc-auditor --since <date>`. Outcome classification is derived from the artifact's tick fields (audits_processed empty + tier_a_commits empty + debt_filed empty → empty; debt_filed non-empty + tier_a_commits empty → debt_only; tier_a_commits non-empty → tier_a_apply).
methodology.input_path_on_office2: /data/services/openclaw/felix-doc-auditor-driver/last-tick.json (snapshot per tick) OR systemd journal SUMMARY lines
methodology.reduction_formula: effective_post_input = post_input_tokens - (post_cache_hit_input_tokens * 0.9); reduction_pct = ((pre_input_tokens - effective_post_input) / pre_input_tokens) * 100. Pre-rework path did NOT use prompt caching, so the discount only applies to the post-rework side. The 0.9 factor reflects Anthropic's ~10% billing rate for cache hits vs cache writes/standard input.
methodology.outcome_classification: Deterministic from `tick.tier_a_commits`, `tick.debt_filed`, `tick.audits_processed` fields in last-tick.json (no heuristic regex needed, unlike pre-rework which had to regex the closing assistant text).
methodology.sample_size_guidance: Target ≥3 samples per outcome over a 72-hour natural-traffic window. If `tier_a_apply` doesn't appear naturally, an operator-driven synthetic audit (file a low-stakes Doc audit issue against a doc whose `last_validated` is stale by ≥30 days) is acceptable; document the synthetic origin in the sample note.
methodology.pre_rework_reference: Pre-rework baseline (felix-doc-auditor-pre-rework.json) was measured against OpenClaw session JSONL via per-tick boundary regex. Post-rework path replaces that surface with the driver's deterministic tick-signal artifact — strictly more accurate (per-judgment counts, no heuristic outcome classifier).
